title: What is known about 1RB0LE_0LC0RF_1LD1LC_1RA0RD_0LA1LA_1RD---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_0LC0RF_1LD1LC_1RA0RD_0LA1LA_1RD---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. The head sweeps across the whole tape, which holds runs of one to three 1s with short gaps and no visible repeating word. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the exact way a halt would happen (D>0 0 1 1, D moving right) and that the other way in is harmless; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 1011 steps, and the halting pattern never comes close to appearing. No invariant that excludes it is known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: A with 0 under the head, 1 right, 1 two right. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: How a halt comes about
claims.text: F reading 1 is the only halt. F is entered only from B reading 1 and B only from A reading 0 (enter_F, enter_B), so the machine halts exactly at A>0 1 1. A is entered from D reading 0 and from E (enter_A); the E way is harmless, so a halt needs D>0 0 1 1 (halt_D).

claims.title: The way in through E is harmless
claims.text: E is entered only from A reading 1, which writes 0 and steps left. Whatever E and A do next, the B or F that follows lands on a cell that has just been written with 0, so it does not halt. Proved for every surrounding tape.

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: For every n and every surrounding tape: C crosses 1^n to the left; D erases 1^n moving right; moving left, A turns (1 1)^n into (1 0)^n and erases (1 0)^n, and E turns (1 1)^n into (0 1)^n.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator (tools/c/tm.h) runs 1011 steps from blank tape without a halt; the visited tape then spans 502,209 cells, 129,978 of them 1.

claims.title: What D sees when it reads 0
claims.text: In the first 2·109 steps D reads 0 about 243 million times. The next three cells are 0 1 0 (79%), 1 1 1, 0 0 0 (10% each), rarely 1 1 0, 1 0 0, 0 0 1 or 1 0 1, and never the halting 0 1 1. A reads 0 in front of 1 1 never.

claims.title: No regular words
claims.text: At the sweep ends the tape is runs of 1, 2 or 3 ones with gaps of 1 to 8 zeros, and short repeats such as (1 1 0 1)^k and (0 1 0)^k, but no word that repeats across the tape.

claims.title: Growth shape
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.507). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.499).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. A proof would have to show that D, moving right, never reads a 0 followed by 0 1 1. The tape looks irregular and no invariant for it is known. Window CTL up to 7 cells and n-gram CPS (widths up to 9, see the README for the larger runs) fail.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine has run 10<sup>11</sup> steps without stopping. Its head sweeps across a tape of short, irregular runs of 1s. This page runs the real machine in your browser and shows the one pattern that would make it stop.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
The other way in is harmless.
243 million times D read 0, never before 0 1 1.

sections.heading: Sweeps over short runs
html: The head crosses the whole tape and adds about one cell at each end per sweep. The tape is runs of one to three 1s with short gaps. Lean proves the straight stretches for any length (lean/Rules.lean), for example

D> 1 1 1          →   0 0 0 D>         (D erases moving right)
1 1 1 1 A>1       →   A>1 1 0 1 0      (A thins out pairs moving left)
1 1 1 C>1         →   C>1 1 1 1        (C crosses 1s moving left)

sections.heading: The one way to halt
html: The only missing transition is F reading 1. F is entered only from B reading 1, and B only from A reading 0, so the machine halts at A>0 1 1. A is entered from E (moving left) or D (moving right). E is entered only when A reads a 1 and writes 0 over it; the B or F that follows lands on that 0, so the E way is safe. That leaves
All of this is proved in Lean for every surrounding tape (lean/Halt.lean). In the simulation the three cells after D's 0 are almost always 0 1 0, 1 1 1 or 0 0 0, and never 0 1 1.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.507). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.499).
After 109 steps the tape spans 50,405 cells (11,531 left of the start, 25,499 right), with a density of 1s of 0.527.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Bouncer over an irregular tape of short 1-runs; it halts only if D, moving right, reads 0 0 1 1, and in 2*10^9 steps the cells after D's 0 have never been 0 1 1.
